- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) and price drops, model often undercorrects; add 1–2% buffer to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, forecast should not drop below 10% below recent low.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to sentiment volatility; use sentiment-weighted average (e.g., 0.7×sentiment + 0.3×price history) to dampen noise.
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model often misreads sentiment as bullish; reduce forecast by 2–5% if sentiment >0.7 and price < previous 3-day average.
